claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
High-temperature oxidation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr causes degradation of its mechanical properties.
The proposed intervention is deposition of an approximately 100 nm Al2O3 coating by ALD at approximately 300 °C.
ALD will produce a continuous, dense alumina layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The ALD alumina layer will adhere robustly to HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited alumina barrier will be self-healing.
A thin, dense protective surface film can impede direct interaction between a metal and its environment.
Alumina's high melting point and low oxygen diffusivity will allow the approximately 100 nm film to persist at 1000 °C.
The alumina film will prevent rapid oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
Suppressing oxygen ingress will minimize detrimental internal-oxide formation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Minimizing internal oxidation will preserve the alloy's tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
Depositing the alumina coating at approximately 300 °C will not alter the alloy's intrinsic microstructure.
The coated alloy will have markedly better oxidation resistance than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
The coating will cause minimal, if any, loss of tensile ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will cause minimal, if any, loss of yield strength relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
